answer: Reef-anchored nonce chaining. Each identity must submit a fresh proof-of-work whose seed includes the previous block's hash plus a hardware-timed latency sample, so no solution can be copied or precomputed across identities. A canyon of sequential dependencies forms: identity N's credential only validates after N-1's unique nonce lands. Duplicating an identity forces the attacker to redo the full chain serially, paying real compute and wall-clock delay per clone. Any ripple of parallel forgery collapses because out-of-order nonces are rejected.
